question: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita Bill, 2023 introduced by ______ ministry in 2023.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita Bill, 2023**, was introduced by the Ministry of Home Affairs in 2023.
 
• This bill aims to replace the colonial-era **Code of Criminal Procedure** (**CrPC**), 1973, with updated provisions to enhance the criminal justice system in India.
 
• The bill introduces mandatory forensic investigations for offenses punishable with seven years of imprisonment or more, along with provisions for electronic trials and proceedings.
 
• It seeks to **digitize **the entire process from **FIR to judgment**, ensuring **transparency** and **efficiency **in criminal proceedings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA):** The MHA oversees internal security, border management, and the administration of Union Territories in India.
 
• **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973:** The CrPC is the primary legislation that outlines the procedures for administering criminal law in India.
 
• **Forensic Investigation:** Involves applying scientific methods to investigate crimes and gather evidence.
 
• **Electronic Trials:** Use of digital platforms and tools for conducting legal proceedings to enhance accessibility and efficiency.
 
• The introduction of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita Bill, 2023, demonstrates the government's commitment to modernizing the **criminal justice system** and addressing contemporary needs with technological advancements.
